tweets.text:
Current AI market sentiment reminds me of crypto post 2018/2022 blow ups:

Degens on leverage totally wiped out but those sitting in spot are HOPING for a rally.

Hoping but not actually buying more themselves. 

They're maxed out. Fully deployed.

Check comments on Reddit or X. Leveraged degens are putting their last cash into the market...

... but it's not enough to offset the late sellers who just want to 'save what they still have left'

Sentiment is mixed between "AI trade is done" with others "It's just a dip".

For a true bubble, there can't be 50/50. We need max mania for that.

Looking at indexes, the market looks not much down, but individual altcoins (I mean AI stocks) are down bad:

$CRWV: -75.2%
$ORCL: -66.4%
$ARM: -61.4%
$INTC: -60.5%
$NBIS: -56.8%
$MU: -45.0%
$AVGO: -40.7%
$AMD: -31.8%
$TSLA: -28.2%
$PLTR: -24.7%
$NVDA: -23.3%

If crypto scenario plays out, first degen stocks go down, and then the majors start to drop. They were holding quite ok until recently.

Then we have institutional funds that one by one go belly up:

We all know about Situational Awareness but more bodies are surfacing - $17B Walleye Capital hedge fund just returned capital.

It takes time for true damage to surface.

And like in crypto, the bad news keep hitting one after another.

Today we have NVDA but tomorrow there'll be something else. 

Because there's always something else when degens start to really look into it while before they would close their eyes and ignore bad news.

Like NVDA CEO news being shared a year ago.

Worse, is that good news will stop having the bullish affect while bad news get blown out of proportions.

You can't fight the wind of change.

Anyway, it's just my crypto experience since 2018 giving these vibes. 

I could be wrong but recently I'm reading books on 1840s railway mania and Andrew's Ross 1929.

No matter the 'narrative du jour' the human psychology stays the same

I’ve been tied up with family issues for the last week (always happens at the worst time), so have only really been able to sit down and look at things properly today.

A few thoughts:

BTC has put in five red weeklies in a row, closed below the 50W MA, and is well within the previous range with the bottom of said range being 60k. It's been hammered with endless bad news and headlines. 

Doesn't feel great, obviously. 

In 2023 when we exited the bear market we saw a sharp drop to the 200DMA and that was bought up and we continued our ascent. We were very close to that level this morning but didn’t quite tag (maybe front run). It sits at $73.2k right now. This was a test I have been expecting as an inevitability since we had our impulse candle.

Buying the 200DMA post bear market exit (if this is that moment) is some of the best execution you could have had and a plan that could be blindly followed without letting outside bias prejudice you.

As an analyst, I can see the other side of the coin: in the context of that previous exiting of bear market moment in 2023 we didn’t have so much sustained weakness, and were above the previous point of breakdown, whereas this time we are below the May highs which is where we broke down from this year.

Not getting the push higher to the 90s has meant we have corrected back into the range, and made this look far more like a deviation rather than a strong exiting of the bear market moment.

Will the bulls step in here at/close to the 200DMA? tbc, there are juicy targets below which seem like they have a realistic shot of hitting now that you finally have indexes likely heading for multi week/multi month correction.

It is a do or die level, as nothing good happens when you accept below the 200DMA. You want to see strength and interested buyers here right now. 

The next best thing if that level fails would be a weekly close no lower than 66k to set a nice macro higher low, would also look like an inverse head and shoulders, which is a good bottoming pattern. Monthly is still bullish and painting this picture. I would very much prefer to not go lower than that. 

I still think the macro bottom is in for Bitcoin, but whenever you accept and linger in a previous range you open up the possibility of the range low hitting (60k) and if that hits, alongside mass panic, does it hold? 

To create new lows you would need a lot of forced selling to happen. Think this could only occur if Saylor gets into trouble, or something similar (always possible ofc). 

We had the set up for Bitcoin to show strength, but ultimately we have fallen back into the range on a sustained basis. This needs to reverse asap for a chance of fucking over the bears. Can't be any delays here.

Good alts will bottom first, as they have been doing. We have so few of them, so it's fairly easy to keep a small watchlist. You can simply ignore everything else. It is a total waste of time and energy and it's all legacy garbage, vapour and failed ideas. Retail and institutions are not coming to buy any of that. 

Either we bottom here, and everything looks pretty damn good in ~6 months.

Or we bottom lower, and everything looks pretty damn good in ~12 months.

I find very few assets attractive when looking forward 5 years from now due to the uncertainty that exists with AI and how long the secular bull has been going. I get the anxiety around AI/quantum for BTC (hence why I also like ZEC), but once it overcomes that it remains one of the few assets that reprices vs everything else given enough time due to sovereign fiscal irresponsibility (not something I see changing). I still see it as a cornerstone asset in a non degen portfolio for the world we currently inhabit.

We are more than a year past the top, so don’t get cute and don't overcomplicate it. Build your exposure and let time do the rest.

This original deck is much better than the other one. But one stark difference here is that your old deck tries to raise significantly more money. And that materially changes the consideration.

This type of compilers / devtools co also historically has large market risk. So it seems to me that you think you can't raise because you're raising a massive amount for your risk category (feels like you're trying to do a neolab raise without being one and no a bit of formal verification research and founders with a research bg doesn't make you a neolab like opportunity). If you dialed it back to a traditional 2m seed, I think you'd find someone to bite. And if you went aggressive like a 5-8m yc style seed without going through yc, you might succeed there too.
